title: VideoLoom: A Video Large Language Model for Joint Spatial-Temporal Understanding
claim: A multi-stage automated annotation pipeline composes off-the-shelf models to produce spatially and temporally grounded labels from raw video.
layout: 2 columns: left vertical stage flow, right two detailed boxed sub-pipelines
description: The figure shows a four-stage video annotation pipeline. The left column is a vertical flow with arrows. It starts with a tennis video filmstrip, then Shot Partition (PySceneDetect and KTS), then Spatial Mask Annotation (blue box), then Shot Merging with Adjacent Tracklets, then Temporal Action Annotation (pink box). The right column expands two of the stages in rounded boxes. The blue Spatial Mask Annotation panel takes the longest shot, runs G-DINO to detect the main character, then Pixel2Cap and SAM2 to generate and propagate masks across the whole video. Shots without a tracklet are filled in with a grounding-tracking loop of G-DINO and SAM2. The pink Temporal Action Annotation panel adds visual prompts (SoM, NumPro frame numbers) to each shot, then Gemini2.5pro produces captions aligned with frame IDs. Video frames from tennis footage are used throughout, with dashed boxes around the text outputs.
caption: Illustration of the designed data annotation pipeline, comprising four stages: shot partition, spatial mask annotation, shot merging, and temporal action annotation. During spatial mask annotation, main characters and their complete tracklets are identified. In temporal action annotation, actions of characters are temporally grounded with visual prompts.
abstract: This paper presents VideoLoom, a unified Video Large Language Model (Video LLM) for joint spatial-temporal understanding. To facilitate the development of fine-grained spatial and temporal localization capabilities, we curate LoomData-8.7k, a human-centric video dataset with temporally grounded and spatially localized captions. With this, VideoLoom achieves state-of-the-art or highly competitive performance across a variety of spatial and temporal benchmarks (e.g., 63.1 J&F on ReVOS for referring video object segmentation, and 48.3 R1@0.7 on Charades-STA for temporal grounding). In addition, we introduce LoomBench, a novel benchmark consisting of temporal, spatial, and compositional video-question pairs, enabling a comprehensive evaluation of Video LLMs from diverse aspects. Collectively, these contributions offer a universal and effective suite for joint spatial-temporal video understanding, setting a new standard in multimodal intelligence.
